source.citation: Zhao H-r, Wang F-c, Yue J, et al. Targeting the Thy-1 mechanotransduction regulator rescues regenerative wound healing and induces hair follicle neogenesis under high tension. Cellular and Molecular Life Sciences. 2026.

causal_route.compact: MECHANICAL_TENSION -> THY1 -> p38MAPK -> TGF_BETA -> ALPHA_SMA + COLLAGEN_I_III -> HYPERTROPHIC_SCAR
causal_route.intervention: local rAAV-mediated Thy-1 knockdown or overexpression
causal_route.in_vivo_support: Thy-1 knockdown under high-tension conditions reduced scar area, improved collagen organization, lowered p38MAPK phosphorylation, TGF-beta, alpha-SMA, Collagen I and Collagen III, and shifted healing toward appendage-containing regeneration.
causal_route.orthogonal_pathway_test: In vitro, p38MAPK inhibitor SB203580 attenuated the pro-fibrotic downstream phenotype driven by Thy-1 overexpression.
causal_route.adapter_boundary: The precise molecular adaptor linking GPI-anchored Thy-1 to p38MAPK remains unresolved; the route is supported at pathway-dependence level, not as a fully mapped direct molecular chain.

timing.tension_schedule: device expanded 2 mm every other day for 14 consecutive days
timing.author_stated_limitation: The authors explicitly describe the three-week pre-wound rAAV schedule as a preconditioning strategy and call for future therapeutic-window studies.

outcomes.scar: reduced area and flatter/softer gross scar phenotype with more orderly collagen organization
outcomes.regeneration: de novo hair follicles and sebaceous glands in the Thy-1 knockdown condition at late follow-up

janus_classification.reason: The intervention precedes injury by three weeks and is molecular rather than a delayed direct physical retuning of an established repair state.

next_action: Search for post-establishment intervention in an independent tissue; do not promote this study into the delayed EXIT CLOCK.
